title: Matthew 7:6
context: Between the ban on hypocritical judgment and the invitation to ask, seek, and knock, Jesus adds a brief word of holy prudence: do not cast what is sacred before those who will only trample and turn violent.

verses.text: “Do not give dogs what is holy, and do not throw your pearls before pigs, lest they trample them underfoot and turn to attack you.
verses.arminianNotes:
After calling for humble self-examination, Jesus warns against naive exposure of holy things. “Dogs” and “pigs” are vivid images for contemptuous hostility, not labels for people we dislike. Wisdom and love together: do not fuel scoffing that only hardens and harms.

Classical Arminians hear responsible stewardship of the gospel. Grace makes us eager to share; prudence keeps us from casting pearls where they will only be crushed. Shared ground: holiness is precious, and discernment is part of love.
verses.reformedNotes:
The saying balances 7:1–5. Mercy toward a brother is not the same as handing holy things to those who despise them. Jesus trains discernment without licensing contempt.

Reformed accent: the church guards Word and sacrament as gifts of the King. Prudence is not unbelief; it is reverence under providence—refusing to treat the holy as cheap fodder for mockery.
verses.keyContrast: Both affirm holy prudence without canceling evangelistic love. Arminians often stress grace-enabled discernment in how we share; Reformed readers often stress reverence for sacred gifts entrusted to the church under Christ’s lordship.
